description: Voice capture from a Pocket recorder, routed into your own trackers. Copy this file to schema.json, then edit the tables and vocabulary to match how you talk.
_comment_starter: Each table is a tracker. Add one by adding an object here and deploying; there is no migration, because every table lives in the same D1 table as JSON. Select fields need no preset choices: a new one exists the moment it is used.
_comment_routing: Pocket records everything - meetings, calls, pocket-dials. A recording that never addressed the system is dropped. confirmIgnoreBelow is how sure the planner must be that a recording was NOT meant for the system before dropping it silently; below that it asks over Telegram first. Set it high and every stray recording pings you until you stop reading the pings, which loses the real ones too. Set it low and a genuine capture disappears with no trace. minConfidenceToWrite is the separate question of how sure it must be about WHERE something goes.
_comment_corrections: Only fields the planner actually wrote are correction candidates, minus lifecycle fields - otherwise checking off a todo teaches the planner to mark new todos done. Routing and classification edits are the signal; using your own database is not.
_comment_reminders: Morning Telegram reminders. events: about a month before a recurring event, every past year's learnings for it, triggered monthsAfter months after the newest adventure that has optInField ticked. onThisDay: the journal entry from exactly N years ago.

tables.name: Journal
tables._comment_candidateFields: Shown to the planner alongside each candidate so an update can merge rather than clobber - it needs to see the gratitudes already on today's row before rewriting the field.
conventions: Gratitudes go one per line in the Gratitudes field, no numbering or bullets - just the things. Record only what they actually said; never invent one to round out a list.
Gratitudes are often recorded on their own ('Gratitudes. Coffee, the walk this morning, a friend calling') rather than inside a full entry. That is still this table.

One row per day. If a Journal record already exists for the recording's date, update that record instead of creating a second one - a gratitudes recording in the evening belongs on the same row as the morning's entry. Only set the fields this recording actually provides; never overwrite a field it says nothing about.
When updating a row that already has Gratitudes, include the existing ones alongside the new - an update replaces the field wholesale.

fields.name: Date
fields.description: PRIMARY. One row per day.

fields.name: Date
fields.description: PRIMARY.

tables.name: Adventure Learnings

fields.name: Adventure Name
fields.description: PRIMARY. The trip or event, as they name it out loud.

fields.name: Learnings
fields.description: A bulleted list that grows - each recording about this adventure appends one.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: The recurring event this belongs to, without the year: Burning Man 26 → Burning Man. Empty for a one-off.

conventions: One row per adventure. A learning about one that already exists is appended to it, never a new row - match on the name as they said it, allowing for speech-to-text mangling.
Event names the recurring event an adventure belongs to, without the year: 'Burning Man 26' is Event 'Burning Man'. Reuse an existing Event when it is plausibly the same one; a one-off trip has none.

Tick Remind me next year for a recurring event, so next year's reminder carries these learnings forward. When creating an adventure under an Event, copy the answer from that Event's previous adventures.

tables.name: To-Dos

fields.name: Title
fields.description: PRIMARY. The task, as a short imperative.

conventions: Due Date is a plain date. Turn what they said into one using the recording's date: 'by Friday' is the coming Friday, 'tomorrow' is the day after the recording. Leave it empty when no deadline was said.
When they say a task is finished ('I called the insurance company', 'mark the flights done'), update that existing to-do with Done = true. Never create a new to-do for something already on the list.

tables.name: Thoughts
tables.description: Loose thoughts and ideas, captured out loud.
conventions: Thought is the thought itself in one line - their words, tightened, not a label about the thought. 'Onboarding should start before the contract is signed', not 'Idea about onboarding'.
For a short thought, Thought alone is the whole record; leave Notes empty rather than restating it.
For a longer one, Thought is the line that would remind them of it later, and Notes carries the reasoning as they said it.
This is the catch-all. Only route here when nothing more specific fits - a thought about an upcoming trip belongs in Adventure Learnings, a thing to do belongs in To-Dos.

fields.name: Thought
fields.description: PRIMARY. The thought in one line.

fields.name: Notes
fields.description: The fuller version, when there is one.

tables.name: Capture Log
tables.description: One row per Pocket recording the system acted on: the dedupe record, the audit trail, and the Review queue in one place.

fields.name: Recording ID
fields.description: PRIMARY. Pocket's recording id. Dedupe key - webhook delivery is at-least-once.

fields.name: Raw Transcript
fields.description: Verbatim, never edited. Any bad write is recoverable by re-running the planner over this.

fields.name: Status
fields.description: Needs review, Unrouted and Failed are the app's Review queue. Ignored rows are recordings that never addressed the system.

fields.name: Target Record ID
fields.description: The row this recording created or appended to.

fields.name: Planner Output
fields.description: JSON the planner emitted. Diffed nightly against the target row to detect manual corrections.

fields.name: Field Snapshot
fields.description: What was actually written, per target record. The nightly sweep diffs the live record against this to spot edits made by hand; after recording them it rewrites the snapshot, so each edit is learned once rather than re-detected forever. Planner Output stays the untouched audit record.

fields.name: Swept At
fields.description: When the correction sweep last diffed this row. Sorting by it ascending rotates the sweep through every row instead of re-checking the newest few forever - blanks sort first, so a row is never checked twice before every other row has been checked once.

fields.name: Reason
fields.description: 'Unknown classifier' means a tracker was named that does not exist - not that the recording had no classifier, which is dropped.

fields.name: Proposed Action
fields.description: The operation the planner would have run. Approving replays this, so triage is a click not a retype.

fields.name: Redo
fields.description: Tick to re-file this recording on the next poll. Put a table name in Target Table first to force where it goes; leave it blank to let the planner decide again. Cleared automatically once re-filed.

tables.name: Corrections
tables.description: Every correction, however it arrived. The most recent rows go into the planner prompt as few-shot examples.

fields.name: Summary
fields.description: PRIMARY.

fields.name: Source
fields.description: Manual edits are the most informative and the easiest to miss - the nightly diff exists to catch them.

fields.name: Raw Transcript
fields.description: The utterance that produced the original write, without which the example makes no sense.

fields.name: Use As Example
fields.description: Uncheck to keep a correction out of the planner prompt.

tables.name: Pocket Meta
tables.description: System state. Key/value so the Worker can stay stateless.

fields.name: Key
fields.description: PRIMARY.
